nonempty contents

A nonempty<a> is a list<a> that is guaranteed to hold at least one element. It is a mandatory head plus a tail that may be empty, so no value of the type can encode an empty list. Operations that would have to drop the last element return a weaker type — list<a> or maybe<nonempty<a>> — instead of a nonempty<a> that could be empty.

Browse the API reference · read the source · generated by koka 3.2.9,

Usage

module demo

import nonempty

fun main() : console ()
  val nel : nonempty<int> = 1 <:: 2 <:: [3]
  nel.length.println
  nel.map(fn(i) i * 2).list.println

Prints 3 and [2,4,6].

Installation

The flake exposes the library as packages.default, with resolved paths under kokaLibraries for downstream flakes:

nix build .packages.x86_64-linux.default

# resolve the include path for a consumer
includePath=nix eval --raw .kokaLibraries.x86_64-linux.nonempty.includePath
koka -o my-app --include="$includePath" src/main.kk

nix develop opens a shell that builds the library, puts it on the module search path, and writes koka.json, so the example above runs as-is.
